A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all supplied pages are readable. However, both reference Appendices A1/A2 but contain no appendix pages or embedded supplements, preventing comparison of those deferred details.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, geometry, efficiency, and ablation results across four driving datasets.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the work's original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The supplied method description retains the same three-level bilateral grid, luminance guidance, slicing, hierarchical transformation composition, regularization terms, and temporal interpolation procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Waymo, NuScenes, Argoverse, and PandaSet on reconstruction and novel-view synthesis, including human, vehicle, and geometry evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same baseline, appearance-code, single-grid, ChatSim, and StreetGS comparisons. The newly cited works do not participate in the reported experiments.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, training and rendering procedures, grid configurations, and ablation settings are unchanged. Neither PDF supplies the additional dataset specifications deferred to Appendix A2.

E4.justification: Both retain the guidance-resolution, grid-size, and loss ablations, computational-efficiency analysis, affine-transformation distributions, and qualitative cases in Tables 4–5 and Figures 3–6.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and scenario averages without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative result panels are retained. For example, the proposed method's NuScenes reconstruction PSNR, novel-view PSNR, and Chamfer Distance remain 27.69, 24.64, and 1.161, respectively.

T1.justification: The supplied mathematical formulation, grid definitions, slicing expression, transformation composition, and Equations 1–9 are unchanged. No formal result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unifying appearance codes and bilateral grids, reducing floaters, improving geometric accuracy, and demonstrating effectiveness across four datasets.

C2.justification: The interpretations of hierarchical photometric refinement and geometric improvement are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning computational overhead and difficult fast-moving or highly non-rigid objects.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same NVIDIA L40 GPU, grid dimensions, computational measurements, and project/code access information. The same pointers to unavailable appendix implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds four background references: Relightable 3D Gaussians, MagicDrive, STORM, and GS-Occ3D. These enter existing citation groups in the introduction and Section 2.2; the substantive discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes consist of added and renumbered citations and updated arXiv version/date text. The narrative prose, terminology, headings, and section sequence are unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded citation groups cause limited line reflow, and the bibliography is repaginated. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–5 retain their visual content, structure, and placement, apart from citation-label updates.

improvement.justification: The four added background citations modestly broaden attribution without substantive discussion or changes to the methods, experimental evidence, exposition, or reproducibility information. The referenced appendices remain absent in both PDFs. The supplied material therefore supports no meaningful overall quality difference.
